q: What is the carbon footprint of elastane (spandex) yarn?
title: Elastane yarn carbon footprint
short: Elastane is a polyurethane fibre spun from petrochemical raw materials, so purchased chemicals are most of its footprint. Your own share is spinning, solvent recovery and heat setting energy. A garment with 5 percent elastane carries that share of the fibre's footprint.
audience: Elastane producers, covering mills and stretch fabric makers

ul: Scope 3: polyols, diisocyanates and solvent purchased.
Scope 1 and 2: spinning, drying and solvent recovery energy.
Solvent losses: count any that are greenhouse gases; most are not.

p: Weight the fibre figures by blend: 95 percent cotton and 5 percent elastane means 0.05 kg of elastane per kg of fabric.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
